transcript.text: What's the difference between a $100,000
CEO, a $1 million CEO, a $10 million
CEO, and a $100 million CEO? A $100,000
CEO is just calling themselves a CEO,
but they are just a solopreneur and they
are working to do the stuff and they're
getting paid for it. They're managing
themselves. A $1 million CEO has a core
team of maybe three to five people,
maybe a contractor here or there, and
they are the ones that are still driving
almost all of the revenue. A $10 million
CEO has a layer of leaders underneath.
So, we're talking directors, maybe
managers a mix at that level, and they
have given away some level of the
conversion and likely the delivery of
the core product, but they're still
integrally involved in the strategy of
all of those things. A $100 million CEO
has executives who are very experienced
in this specific business and are
driving because of their own incentives
for each of those lines of business, and
all of the decision-making has been
pushed down, and the CEO is only guiding
the incentive structure, both direct in
terms of money and indirect in terms of
character and the cultural values of the
business to align the output of every
one of those divisions towards the
ultimate vision of the business.
